facts.fact: The Centre of Excellence for CRVS Systems case study states that the Department of Civil Registration of the Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration registers births and deaths through its regional directorate, and that the Office of the Prime Minister develops and maintains the NPRS; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that from 2000 the Office of the Prime Minister, with the ministry, designed and built the NPRS locally using internal resources, and calls it a homegrown register built with internal resources; it gives no budget figure, and the published date is used.

The case study states that a five-year civil registration and vital statistics strategic plan was drafted in 2014 by the ministry with the Namibia Statistics Agency, and that the e-Government Strategic Action Plan 2014 to 2018, led by the Office of the Prime Minister, treats an interoperable NPRS as a key part of the e-government vision.
The case study's timeline gives the birth registration module of the NPRS as designed and piloted in the Khomas Region in 2011.

The case study's timeline gives the death module of the NPRS as designed and deployed in 2012 and the birth registration module as deployed nationwide in 2013, with the marriage module in 2014; the civil registration system was built on the identity platform step by step from 2010 to 2014.

The case study states that the workstations used to enter registered information electronically are permanently linked with the NPRS, allowing real-time data communication and electronic validation, and that registration is completed at a ministry office, including the birth registration office at the health facility; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that the ministry has a network of 55 offices across the country (14 regional offices, 23 hospital-based facilities and 18 sub-regional offices, 9 of which enrol for identity documents) and still works with a few magistrate courts on birth and death registration; it gives no separate count of offices entering records in the NPRS, and the published date is used.
